representation_hypothesis: biology is the observation after inverse acquisition transport, not an independently decoded peer channel

architecture.candidate_operator: T_theta(x)=c+Q^T(exp(H theta) elementwise * Q(x-c)); Q orthogonal
architecture.control_operator: same tensors and parameter count, but log-scale=tanh(H theta), retaining identity/inverse while breaking additive closure
architecture.reference_gauge: scanner 0 acquisition coordinate fixed to zero

new_synthetic_benchmark.heldout_relation: scanner_5 = scanner_1 composed with scanner_2 relative to scanner_0

primary_falsification.name: heldout composition prediction
primary_falsification.rule: using no scanner-5 training cells, predict scanner 5 from an unseen-identity scanner-0 observation using the learned scanner-1 and scanner-2 acquisition operators
primary_falsification.control_prediction: same coordinate-sum rule through the parameter-matched nonclosed operator

requirements: candidate and control parameter counts exactly equal
candidate heldout-composition improvement versus no transport has lower 95% bootstrap bound > 0 in every renderer/seed
candidate mean biological-latent recovery R2 from canonical representation >= 0.80
control-minus-candidate heldout-composition MSE lower 95% bootstrap bound > 0
control-minus-candidate heldout-scanner canonical MSE lower 95% bootstrap bound > 0

claim_boundary: A pass establishes only that explicit feature-space group transport supports reusable factorization and heldout composition on this new synthetic mechanism benchmark. It does not establish that real scanners obey this group family.
future_real_data_test_if_promoted: prospectively freeze v3, then evaluate five-scanner paired data using reference-gauge canonicalization, direct versus composed relative transport, unseen-scanner transport, scanner leakage, biological retention, and matched unstructured transport controls without pretending any real scanner is physically a composition of two others.
